title: Music dips under the speech by itself
goal: A music bed added under a talking recording plays at full level over the voice, and the only fix today is dragging four level points around every sentence. The captions already know exactly when someone is talking, so the music can dip under the speech in one step, the way Premiere's auto ducking and the audio mock do.
notes: docs/design/video-audio.md section 7 cut 'Duck music under voiceover' on 2026-09-21 because 'it needs the app to know which layer is a voice'. That has changed: captions now write themselves with word-level timing (the captions track, CaptionCue / TranscribedWord), so the spoken stretches are known. The level model already represents a duck as points either side of a dip (Sources/PhotonzCore/AudioMix.swift:12-14, 41, 157, 277), and walks already have a .soundDuck step (PlaytestScript.swift:1231). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-audio.html (Duck toggle :326, menu row 'Duck music under voiceover' :101, Ducking section :626-632). Competitors: Premiere Essential Sound auto-ducking, Final Cut's audio ducking, Descript. New visible command, so it went through a card first (manager prompt rule). Filed by the 2026-10-05 evening manager pass.
acceptance: One command, Duck Under Speech, on the music's right-click and in the Clip menu, makes the dip (settled on 2026-10-20, when the waiting cards were taken as recommended)

On a recording whose captions have written themselves, with music added from Sequence, the music sits lower under every stretch of speech and comes back up in the gaps, as level points on the music's bar that can be dragged afterwards like any other
A sound with no captions anywhere in the document says so (the row is dimmed with a tip saying captions are needed) rather than doing nothing
The dip is heard in playback and in the exported MP4: a test reads the exported music level inside and outside a spoken stretch
Try it: open the sample talk, let captions write, Sequence > Add Media at Playhead and pick a music file, then right-click the music and choose Duck Under Speech. Audit written under queue/audits/
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: decision "When you put music under someone talking, should it dip under their voice by itself?" resolved: One command, Duck Under Speech (Taken as recommended: the user, 2026-10-19, said there were too many cards, most did not matter and they could not follow them. Change it later only if they complain about the result)
digest 2026-10-20: goal and checklist rewritten to build the card's answer; the card items are gone, since the answer is in

Adversarial pass before building: the captions' word timings come out end to end, so only real gaps of a second or more open the duck; short breaths stay down, which also stops pumping. The voice itself is never offered the command (it would duck itself): left out on the voice the captions were heard off, detached or not.

Chose replacing the line's points (keeping fades) over adding to them because re-running after captions change must not stack a second duck, and Premiere's Generate Keyframes replaces too. One undo restores the old line.
Chose moving Reset Gain under More on a sound clip over raising the 11-row menu limit because the limit is the user's 2026-10-17 rule and Reset Gain only shows once gain was changed.
Chose the mock's -8 dB / 300 ms and a 1.1 s shortest pause (two ramps plus 0.5 s at full) so a pause opens only when the music can sit up for half a second.

left rough: dips are written once and do not follow the voice when it moves (mock: 'a relationship, not a baked edit'); the answered card chose a command, so not filed. Amount/ramp adjustable only by dragging points; not filed (no user ask). The sample talk has no pause over 0.3 s, so the walk lifts 0:04-0:08 out to show a gap.

Verified: SpeechDuckingTests (12), SpeechDuckExportTests (real MP4 from DocumentMovieWriter, music read back down under both spoken stretches and up in the pause), TimelineMenuTableTests, AgentReach and menu-bar tests; Scripts/test.sh exit 0; walks music-ducks-under-the-speech-walk (no flags, not in front) and duck-under-speech-from-the-clip-menu-walk (front) both ok. Opened 2-ducked-sc.png: the line sits low under both talk pieces and rises through the lifted gap, 6 points on the bar.

Duck Under Speech on a sound clip's right-click, its level line's right-click and the Clip menu: music dips -8 dB under every spoken stretch the captions heard, as draggable level points; dimmed with a tip with no captions. Core in SpeechDucking.swift; verified by SpeechDuckingTests, an MP4 export test reading the music level back, Scripts/test.sh green, and two walks (no flags).
